correctness.rationale: The product formula gives \(A^2=\operatorname{span}\{v,w\}\) with dimension \(2\) and \(\operatorname{Ann}(A)=0\). For every integer \(t\ge2\), the displayed basis has nonzero determinant and zero mixed products. Rank preservation in the pencil \(\operatorname{span}\{q_1,q_2\}\) forces an automorphism to scale \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) separately; coefficient comparison then forces every scalar to be \(1\). The proof is algebraic and covers all \(t\) and all rational automorphisms.

value.rationale: The result isolates a natural rigidity boundary: an algebra with no nonidentity automorphisms, \(\operatorname{Aut}(A)=\{I\}\), can still have infinitely many natural-basis equivalence classes. The exact trivial-group condition is a meaningful strengthening of finite-but-nontrivial symmetry examples, and the proof is explicit rather than experimental.
